doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bird memories, cabaret card and Prestige years
title: Session length and twelve takes of Portrait of Jackie
summary: A Prestige date ran about three hours; Mingus made McLean record Portrait of Jackie twelve times in a row and then used the first take.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: You say you remember the September – the Mobley’s Message, Jackie McLean Sextet day. What do you remember about that day?
I knew that it was a doubleheader, a day where I was going to be able to get some money. We had our stuff already rehearsed. So we went in and made that recording.
How long would a recording session take? As long as it takes to cut the tunes?
I mean, two hours? One hour? Three hours?

Maybe three hours. If we had the stuff down and went in and did it within one or two takes, we’d be out of there in three hours or more. But if we ran into a problem, sometimes where – like I remember when Mingus made me record Portrait of Jackie
maybe 12 times. After I did it the twelfth time, when he listened to it and the record came out, I say, “Charlie, which one of those takes did you take?” Right.
There’s something obsessive about Charles Mingus. Would you say?

Yeah man. “Do it again.” I was so sick of that tune. And I did them in a row. It wasn’t like he took a break and we did some other music and came back to that. I did 12 in a row, the whole thing, solo and everything. I was wiped. I didn’t want to hear that tune anymore.
